description.narrative: The majority of maternal deaths in Nigeria, like in the rest of the world are preventable, while the causal factors can be multiple and complex governments must also be held accountable when their actions or inaction contribute to this ongoing loss of women’s lives. Since the launch of the Safe motherhood initiative in Nairobi in 1987, numerous goals for reducing maternal mortality have been set, none have been met in Nigeria. In Northwest Nigeria 1,025 women per 100,000 are still dying while giving life. PADEAP’s safe motherhood project aims to reduce maternal mortality in selected LGAs in Katsina State. For safe motherhood strategies to be implemented, advocacy is important in order to create political commitment to safe motherhood. Advocacy is needed not only at policy level and decision making level, but also at community level in order to solicit broad support to safe motherhood. At the community level we will create awareness and demand for services through health education, attempting to address the reasons for low utilisation, including geographical, financial and socio-cultural. At policy level our advocacy work will focus on ensuring women have skilled attendance at delivery, and accessibility of emergency obstetric care (EOC) facilities for women with complications.
